analysis.title: China Economic Activity and Policy Tracker: Nov 6
key_insights: GS now publishes the China activity tracker weekly, instead of less often, to follow the effect of the higher energy price supply shock on Chinese economic activity.
The GS GDP nowcasting model points to 4.6% yoy real GDP growth in 2026Q4.
The PBOC raised the reserve requirement ratio (RRR) for FX deposits by 2pp on November 3, which GS reads as signaling discomfort over rapid RMB appreciation.
CNY depreciated against USD and the CFETS basket over the past week. The US-China yield gap narrowed to 324 bps but remains historically wide.
30-city primary-market property transaction volume fell over the past week, while 16-city secondary-market volume remained stable.
Local government special bond issuance is RMB 3.97tn year-to-date, nearing the year-ago level. Total government bond issuance reached RMB 10.1tn, or 85% of the annual quota.
A larger share of local government bond proceeds may have gone to debt resolution in Jan-Aug 2026. Policy bank support increased in October, led by policy bank bond net issuance.

GS's nowcast puts China oil demand at 16.6mb/d in the latest reading. Visible landed crude inventory continued to edge down, and Brent declined over the past week while domestic gasoline and diesel prices were unchanged.

Official port container throughput declined over the past week and was below year-ago levels. Freight volumes of departing ships at 20 major ports rebounded as activity recovered from typhoon-related disruptions.
On October 31 the PBOC changed its policy rate from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate. The RMB 800bn of new policy-based financial instruments was fully deployed on October 28.
On November 6 the State Council called for faster implementation of major projects and the 'Six Networks', and for support for corporate investment in equipment upgrades and intangible assets.
Consumer confidence edged down: NBS in September and Morning Consult over the past week. Employment PMIs (weighted average) ticked up in October.
Steel demand was stable and steel production edged up over the past week. Coastal-province daily coal consumption edged up. Domestic passenger flights edged down, and traffic congestion ticked up.
Outstanding US soybean export sales to China for the 2026/27 marketing year ticked down in the last week of October. Overnight interbank repo rates edged down.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS's nowcasting model estimates Q4 2026 growth at 4.6% yoy. This is a model estimate, not an official print.
The gap narrowed but remains historically wide, which keeps pressure on the CNY.
GS's high-frequency nowcast of China oil demand rose to 16.6mb/d.
Issuance is well advanced against the full-year quota set in March.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Issuance is nearing the year-ago level.

risk_factors: Higher energy prices as a supply shock to Chinese activity.
Rapid RMB appreciation, which prompted the PBOC to hike the FX deposit RRR.
Weakness in the property market, with 30-city primary transaction volume falling.
Port container throughput below year-ago levels, and typhoon-related disruption to port activity.
A larger share of local government bond proceeds going to debt resolution rather than new investment.
